title: Setup blob storage only when adding cache entries
description:
In the current logic, blob storage bucket is destroyed if it exists but has no cache entries. Looking at the logs we noticed some buckets repeatedly getting deleted. This happens because some users only request cache entries without ever adding new ones.

To fix this, blob storage bucket will now only be created when adding a new cache entry. Subsequent get requests will still work since the blob storage will already exist once an entry is added.

>     - Move blob storage setup to `r.on "caches"` block, ensuring it's only done when adding entries.

title: Avoid using PATCH requests for web routes
description:

I previously handled similar cases using `r.api_patch_web_post`, but that is an ugly name, and this behavior will extend to all future web routes, so it makes sense to change the default `r.patch` behavior. This updates the two `r.api_patch_web_post` calls to use `r.patch`.

While removing the javascript code, I noticed I neglected to remove the inline-edit javascript in a6a8b8b5edc63cbcb2e80cba20346b29e9450f71, so this includes a commit to remove that.

title: Convert web routes to use POST instead of DELETE
description:
This allows all deletion routes to work correctly without
javascript. It significantly simplifies the specs, since they
can use normal Capybara methods instead of page.driver.delete.
This uses the same approach previous used for r.patch.

The second commit is quite large because of how many r.delete
routes we have. I would have liked to split it up, but many parts
are interdependent, and I don't think it's possible if we want the
intermediate commits to pass specs. I tried to do as much possible
work in the first commit, which reorganizes routes without
changing behavior

Here's a breakdown of the different parts:

In helpers/general.rb, override r.delete to operate similarly
to r.patch, where for web routes, it matches POST with an
additional delete segment.

In the routes, for web deletion requests, use r.redirect.
Add flash notices in all places they were missed. Add
handle validation failures in routes that can fail (maybe it
should be added in additional, currently untested cases?).

Special handling for specific routes:

* inference_api_key: Use check_found_object to avoid multiple
  conditionals.

* postgres: For metric destination deletion, mark that no audit log is
  expected if the metric destination does not exist.

* private_location: Update the route structure changes, missed in the
  previous commit.

Change the delete_button component. Drop the csrf_url, redirect, and
method arguments, no longer needed. Add the following optional
arguments:

* exact_url: Set to not append /delete to the URL, used by the private
  subnet disconnect template.

* form_id: Sets the form attribute on the button, associated it with a
  different form than the default one. Used in the token template.
  When this is used, it only adds the button tag, it does not wrap it
  in a form tag.

* icon: Override the icon used. Used in the github runner template.

* hidden_inputs: Use the given hidden inputs in the form. Used in the
  billing template.

* attributes: Customize the attributes used. Used in multiple
  templates.

Most other templates modified in this commit modify only the arguments
passed to the delete_button component, and in most cases, there are
fewer arguments. Some templates needed special handling:

* github runners: Switch from using the button template to the delete
  button component. Inline the destroy_url variable, since it is only
  needed once and not twice.

* users: Add separate form tags for each user and invitations, and
  use the form_id argument to associat the button to those forms. This
  wasn't needed before as javascript was used for submission, but it
  is needed now, as the buttons would otherwise submit the containing
  form (which is used for updating user permissions.

Specs were partially updated by Claude with the following prompt:

```
In the previous commit, I made changes to use the HTTP POST
method instead of the DELETE method for deletion requests from web
browsers. This is to avoid the need to use javascript to submit the
requests. This results in 58 spec failures, which you can see in
`spec.log`. Please update each failing spec to use standard Capybara
testing methods such as `click_button`, instead of the current code
that uses `page.driver.delete`. When updating the specs, always
check for for the expected flash notice using `expect(page).to
have_flash_notice`, and remove any comments related to using
javascript for delete requests.
```

This reduced the number of failing specs from 58 to 33. Remaining
specs were fixed manually, and even in those cases Claude helped
with the cleanup even if it didn't fix the issue completely. This
reduces and simplifies most of the related specs.

Delete a bunch of code from the .delete-btn click function in the
javascript, as it is no longer used.

Best viewed ignoring whitespace.
ellipsis_summary:
Convert deletion routes to use POST instead of DELETE, update related components and specs, and remove unused JavaScript.
> 
>   - **Behavior**:
>     - Change deletion routes to use POST instead of DELETE, adding a "delete" segment for web requests in `helpers/general.rb`.
>     - Add flash notices and handle validation failures in routes like `project.rb`, `billing.rb`, and `github.rb`.
>   - **Components**:
>     - Update `delete_button` component to remove `csrf_url`, `redirect`, and `method` arguments, and add `exact_url`, `form_id`, `icon`, `hidden_inputs`, and `attributes`.
>   - **Specs**:
>     - Update specs in `access_control_spec.rb`, `firewall_spec.rb`, and `inference_api_key_spec.rb` to use `click_button` instead of `page.driver.delete`.
>     - Reduce spec failures from 58 to 33 by updating to standard Capybara methods.
>   - **Misc**:

>

title: Remove unused association methods
description:
Such methods consume unnecessary memory, resulting in longer full garbage collections.

This uses Sequel's unused_associations plugin to detect the unused associations. Unfortunately, there are a number of false positives, due to mocking in the specs. I've flagged those associations so they aren't considered unused, but such flags should be removed after the unnecessary mocking is removed from the specs (and association mocking should always be considered unnecessary).

This runs the unused associations check in CI, so that code will fail CI if it introduces an unused association, or stops using a currently used association without removing it or removing the unused association methods.
ellipsis_summary:
Remove unused association methods and add CI check to prevent future unused associations using Sequel's `unused_associations` plugin.
> 
>   - **Behavior**:

>     - Introduces a CI check using Sequel's `unused_associations` plugin to prevent future introduction of unused associations.
>     - Flags false positives in tests due to mocking, with a note to remove these flags after unnecessary mocking is addressed.
>   - **Implementation**:

>     - Modifies `model.rb` to conditionally load the `unused_associations` plugin based on the `UNUSED_ASSOCIATIONS` environment variable.
>   - **Models**:

title: Add VM host health check to verify clock source is tsc
description:
tsc is the preferred clock source because it is more reliable and precise. Our hosts use tsc by default, but in some cases they may fall back to hpet if issues are detected with tsc.

When a host switches to hpet, it can cause instability and runtime issues for runners. In particular, this leads to errors like "OS monotonic time stepped backwards!", which we've observed frequently in Elixir-based workflow jobs.

We should monitor the clock source on VM hosts and alert if any host switches from tsc to hpet, so we can take corrective action early.

Before, they could rename the created private subnet, but doing so requires knowing the ubid of the created postgres resource, which makes it more challenging to script. This allows for specifying the name up front, so that after creation, you can add firewalls directly to it without parsing the output from other requests/commands.

Mostly written by Claude Code using the following prompt:

I changed the CLI option from `-n` to `-P`, and did some minor refactoring.

title: [destroying #6] Add before_destroy callback to Prog::Base
description:
- **Move Prog::Test2 to a separate file**

Prog::Test2 was in the same file as Prog::Test and inherited from it.

In real progs, we don't use inheritance, and this setup caused
unexpected behavior. For example, it inherited hop_destroy method, but
since @labels is empty, it can't hop there.

It's better to keep it in a separate file and mimic the structure of
real progs.

- **Add before_destroy callback to Prog::Base**

Some progs run cleanup logic (like finalizing billing records) in before_run, but this logic only needs to execute once before hopping to destroy.

The before_destroy runs exactly once before the destroy hop, avoiding the need to duplicate the entire before_run logic.

title: [destroying #7] Pop strand in before_run when prog lacks destroy label
description:
Previously, before_run assumed progs with a destroy semaphore also had a destroy label to hop to. Several progs (BootstrapRhizome, InstallRhizome, ConvergePostgresResource) needed custom before_run implementations to handle the case where they had the semaphore but no destroy label, manually popping the strand instead.

This change moves that logic into the base before_run. When destroy_set? is true but hop_destroy is not defined, pop the strand directly. This eliminates duplicate before_run implementations.

title: [destroying #8] Pop extra stack frames in before_run during destruction
description:
When a strand has multiple frames in its stack and is destroyed, the top frame destroys the associated entities and pops. The next frame then continues to work but fails because the entities are already destroyed. This is fixed by first popping all frames but the last one, then switching to the destroy label to handle cleanup.

Several progs (InferenceEndpointReplicaNexus, InferenceRouterReplicaNexus, InferenceRouterTargetNexus, MinioServerNexus) had custom before_run implementations to handle this case. We added these because we hit the issue before, but any prog that pushes other progs could encounter it. Moving this logic into the base before_run handles it universally.

description:
When we trigger the destroy action for a private subnet, it still appears as “available” until the very end of the process.

Adding a “deleting” state would make it clear that the resource is in the process of being destroyed.

Since this is the first semaphore dependent display state for private subnets, we need to load it eagerly.

title: Display current usage of project in the admin panel
description: - **Add space between object extra in the admin panel** - **Add collapsible table to admin table** Adding new extras to object detail pages makes them longer and harder to find relevant data. When I added current usage data to the project detail page, it became very long. To address this, I added the ability to collapse tables so the data is hidden by default and shown only when needed. This is implemented using the HTML details/summary elements, which is a pure CSS solution. I also introduced a new component instead of adding multiple if/else blocks to the existing table component. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 - **Display current usage of project in the admin panel** 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5

title: Remove the use of :no_association_method association option
description:
The admin site expects that if an association exists, the association method exists. It's currently undertested, but it's likely all models that were using :no_association_method have broken admin pages (at least GitHubInstallation did).

Change the unused_associations_check rake task to not recommend the use of this option, as it currently doesn't recommend the use of :no_dataset_method.

title: Return 400 instead of 500 for invalid Kubernetes version
description: This commit adds proper validation for Kubernetes version parameter that makes the endpoint return a 400 Bad Request with helpful error message instead of throwing a 500.

title: Dump Clover database on E2E tests
description:
Add pg_dump step to capture database state and upload as artifact for debugging.
The pg_dump for now includes an allowlisted subset of tables that's relatively safe to export

New sample run: https://github.com/ubicloud/ubicloud/actions/runs/21042941070

title: Check for PostgresServer#run_query insecurity
description:
This changes PostgresServer#run_query to work similarly to Sshable#cmd, and fail if passed a non-frozen string. To handle cases currently using interpolation, instead of the :placeholder usage, allow passing a Sequel::Dataset, and take the SQL from that (without parameterization, since the full SQL is needed). The Sequel::Dataset can use :placeholders, so this allows for very similar code as used for shell command placeholder escaping.

Have run_query call _run_query, and have the specs override that.

Check that run_query itself is never mocked in the specs.

While non of the interpolated strings appear to be vulnerable, this replaces an insecure pattern with a secure pattern, which should be preferable.

title: Replace mocks with real models in CertNexus spec
description:
The spec used Strand.new (unpersisted) and stubbed nx.cert, nx.dns_zone, and cert column accessors. This made tests brittle and disconnected from actual database behavior.

Now uses the strand returned by assemble, so nx.cert naturally returns the real Cert via subject_is :cert. Association and column stubs are replaced with real model operations.

Remaining 22 mocks are for ACME external service calls (appropriate).

title: Demock postgres_resource_spec
description:
Instance doubles for PostgresResource and PostgresServer disconnected these tests from real database behavior. Schema or association changes would go undetected since mocks don't validate against actual models.

Replace all Sequel model mocks with real persisted instances:
- PostgresResource with associated Strand via postgres_resource let
- PostgresServer via create_postgres_server() helper with real Vm
- Real semaphore operations (incr_destroy) instead of yield stubs
- Proper FK chain: Project → PrivateSubnet → Vm → PostgresServer

The setup_postgres_resource() helper encapsulates the repeated fixture pattern, and create_postgres_server() handles the 10+ line setup for each server instance.

title: Add etcd backups
description:
Introduces the KubernetesEtcdBackup strand and associated logic to
    perform hourly etcd backups and upload them to a MinIO bucket.

    - Model: Add methods to KubernetesEtcdBackup model to check backup
    status, setup_bucket, and retrieve blob storage credentials.
    - Nexus: Create `Prog::Kubernetes::EtcdBackupNexus` to manage the
    backup lifecycle:
        - Sets up blob storage user and policy.
        - Creates the backup bucket.
        - Triggers the backup job periodically.
        - Passes MinIO credentials to the backup script.
    - Rhizome: Add backup-etcd script to:
        - Install `mc` (MinIO Client) idempotently.
        - Clean up old backups to prevent disk accumulation.
        - Capture etcd snapshot using `etcdctl` via `crictl`.
        - Upload the backup to the specified MinIO bucket.
        - Clean up the local backup file after upload.

title: Add admin page to find archived records
description: I often find myself querying the database to find archived records. This is especially painful when working with short-lived resources such as GitHub runners. Being able to look up archived records in the admin panel using an ID from logs would be extremely helpful and save a lot of time. ArchivedRecord table has index on `archived_at` and `model_name` columns, so it's important to filter by those columns in any query on this table. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Every time I saved this file, my editor removed trailing whitespaces on empty lines.

Since our .editorconfig is configured to trim trailing whitespaces, this change simply makes the file consistent with that rule.

I was inspired by Jeremy’s Sshable#write_file helper.

title: Decrease day limits in archived record search page
description:
The page can fetch archived records from the last 15 days in ~4 seconds.

When the number of days is increased, query time grows much faster than linearly. As a result, the request can exceed Heroku’s 30-second router timeout, causing a timeout error on the UI while the query continues running in the background.

title: Fix one_to_one associations that should be many_to_one
description:
In Sequel, one_to_one is only used if there is foreign key in the associated table that references a key in the current table. If the foreign key is in the current table referencing the associated table, then many_to_one should be used, even if the underlying relationship is one-to-one due to database constraints.

The many_to_one/one_to_one distinction mostly doesn't matter for read-only associations, but it should be fixed anyway. It also results in simpler code, since you don't need to override the key/primary_key options when using the correct association type.

title: Use authorization.domain for ACME DNS challenge records
description:
When requesting a certificate with multiple SANs, ACME returns one authorization per domain. Each authorization object contains an identifier field (RFC 8555 Section 7.1.4) specifying which domain it authorizes. The acme-client gem exposes this as authorization.domain.

The previous implementation assumed there was no way to tie an authorization to its domain, so it created DNS challenge records for every authorization across every domain (a cross-product). With 2 domains this created 4 records instead of 2.

This change uses authorization.domain to create exactly one DNS challenge record per authorization, for the correct domain.

Based on https://github.com/ubicloud/ubicloud/tree/jeremy-private-name-ssl-cert

title: Demock postgres_resource_nexus_spec
description:
Replace instance_double(PostgresResource) with real model creation via create_postgres_resource and create_postgres_server helpers, letting Sequel handle all associations.

title: Display workflow job for runner in admin panel
description: We added `workflow_job` to `redacted_columns` because it contains a lot of data and was cluttering logs and pry output. However, since the admin panel relies on `inspect_values` to display object details, this also hides `workflow_job` information there. We can render it as an extra view in the admin panel. This has an added benefit, presenting the data in a structured table makes it much easier to read compared to raw JSON.

title: Elide location_id to keyword shorthand in assemble calls
description:
Ruby 3.1+ allows `key:` as shorthand for `key: value` when a same-named binding exists in scope. This spec has `let(:location_id)` returning `Location::HETZNER_FSN1_ID`, so the 11 call sites passing that constant can use the shorter form.

The shorthand reduces visual noise and clarifies intent: these calls pass through the test fixture's location rather than specifying an independent value.

title: Strip newlines from exception message in E2E summary
description: The exception extraction step was only applying gsub("\n"; " ") to the backtrace line, but exception messages from Postgres errors also contain embedded newlines (e.g., between ERROR and DETAIL sections). These newlines broke the markdown table layout in the GitHub Actions summary. **Before** **After**

title: Rescue all SSH connection errors in VmHostSliceNexus wait state
description:
The wait state was only rescuing Sshable::SshError, missing other connection errors like Net::SSH::ConnectionTimeout. This caused unhandled exceptions instead of gracefully hopping to unavailable.

The fix uses SSH_CONNECTION_ERRORS, consistent with the unavailable state handler in the same file and other progs.
